episode.showDescription: The official podcast of comedian Joe Rogan.
episode.episodeDescription: Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, is a YouTuber, entrepreneur, and philanthropist. He is the founder of Beast Industries and Beast Philanthropy, and the creator and host of the Prime Video competition series “Beast Games.”www.beastgames.comwww.beastphilanthropy.orgwww.youtube.com/@MrBeast Learn more about your ad choices. Visit podcastchoices.com/adchoices

transcript_window.text: And I know the perfect people for it.
For Salesforce, we did their Super Bowl commercial this year.
in the commercial, I hid a million dollars in it.
Basically, if you watch the commercial just with your computer in the commercial, you can win a million dollars.
And there's a bunch of random clues and puzzles hidden through it.
so the first thing it did, it took you to a website that just loosely explained it.
Over 60 million people visited that site and attempted it.
But it still took weeks for people to find the million dollars.
And it was one of the craziest internet puzzle hunts ever because it would take you to this website, which then would take you to this other one where you'd have to call a number.
It's a four -hour voicemail, but at the very end, I would say, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, blah, blah, blah.
And if you weren't recording this, you're going have to listen to all four hours again.
Hang up.
And then it's just sending you everywhere.
And it's basically like 100 of the most complex puzzles on the internet.
And it took this group of really high -level puzzle solvers almost an entire month to solve it.
Wow.
with a million dollars on the line.
And millions of people were trying it, and there's whole subreddit dedicated to it.
And so I just basically went on Reddit and I got all the most cracked out puzzle solvers in the world.
And was like, if you had unlimited budget, how would you make the most insane puzzle ever?
And then that's what they came up with.
And it's hard to even articulate the steps on it.
Some of it was, I don't even know how to describe it.
It was so complicated.
Sometimes there's a page with a bunch of buttons on it, like a million buttons, but only one works.
And you have to go through and click it all.
